clue.text: Letter or card

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a written symbol such as a letter of the alphabet
second meaning: a 'card' is an amusing eccentric person, also called a real one of these

explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter or card' sounds like a choice of things to post; the second meaning is the old slang sense of card as an oddball.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a written symbol and, informally, an eccentric or amusing person.

clue.text: Quark cheese, hardly any remaining from the first minute

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter, which is the only part used
with hardly any left, most of the middle of the cheese's name is dropped, keeping only its ends

parts.note: a hard English cheese
the opening letter of minute

explanation.surface: Quark, a soft cheese, is nearly all gone within a minute of being served.
explanation.walkthrough: Quark looks like the soft cheese, which seems to tie it to 'cheese'; it is the particle physicist's quark. Cheddar loses its middle EDD to leave CHAR, then M follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Charm is one of the six flavours of quark in particle physics, alongside up, down, strange, top and bottom.

clue.text: You had a late dinner we hear, to get thin

indicators.note: what we hear is a spoken phrase, so the letters come from its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: a late dinner is one eaten at ten o'clock

explanation.surface: A remark that eating dinner late is how someone lost weight.
explanation.walkthrough: Said quickly, 'at ten you ate' runs together into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To attenuate is to become thinner, weaker or reduced in force.

clue.text: Ritual performed with zest in battle

indicators.note: a ritual that is performed is acted out afresh, so these letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, 'with' just adding it to the mix

explanation.surface: A ceremony carried out with enthusiasm on a battlefield.
explanation.definitionFit: Austerlitz (1805) is Napoleon's great victory over Austria and Russia, a famous battle.

clue.text: Exposed without a spinner

definitions.meaning: first meaning: bare-breasted, uncovered above the waist
second meaning read literally: lacking a top, the toy that spins

explanation.walkthrough: 'Spinner' suggests a cricket bowler, but here it is the child's spinning toy, and lacking one makes you top-less.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means bare above the waist, and split up it also reads as having no spinning toy.

clue.text: For the third time, decorate small screen?

parts.note: to do up once more after a redo is to re-redo
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: Painting a little screen yet again, the third coat.
explanation.walkthrough: Doing is the first time, redoing the second, so re-redoing is the third.
explanation.definitionFit: A reredos is an ornamental screen or panel behind a church altar.

clue.text: Polish king receives one Cubist

indicators.note: something that receives takes another thing inside it

parts.note: to polish is to rub
K is the chess abbreviation for king
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A Polish monarch welcomes a painter of the Cubist school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' with its capital pretends to be the nationality; it is the verb. Likewise 'Cubist' is not an art movement painter but a cube's inventor.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernő Rubik invented the famous puzzle cube, so he is a cube man in a playful sense.

clue.text: Make hasty tour of one archaeological site?

indicators.note: a tour goes all the way round something, so one word wraps around another

parts.note: to make haste is to run
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Rushing round a dig on a quick sightseeing trip.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that ruins are an example of a site rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient remains such as a ruined temple are typical places archaeologists excavate.

clue.text: Peer round in store

indicators.note: one item placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: a barn is a farm store
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Someone looks around inside a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peer' looks like the verb to look closely; it is the noun for a nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: A baron is the lowest rank of the British peerage, so he is a noble member of the Lords.

clue.text: Show love to workers, as some may on entering office

definitions.text: as some may on entering office

parts.note: a kiss shows affection
hands are manual workers

explanation.surface: A boss is affectionate towards staff, as a new manager might be on their first day.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, new ministers formally kiss hands with the monarch when taking office.
explanation.definitionFit: Kissing the sovereign's hand is the ceremony by which UK prime ministers and ministers accept appointment.

clue.text: Nothing in key signature at first for singers

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it

parts.note: the Alt key on a computer keyboard

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word just before

parts.note: the opening letter of signature
zero, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A musical score lacking a key signature at the start, meant for a choir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key signature' reads as a single musical term, but the words split: a keyboard key, then the opening letter of signature.
explanation.definitionFit: Altos sing the lower female or high male voice part in a choir.

clue.text: Preconceived view of special trip through capital

indicators.note: going through something means being inside it

parts.note: the capital of France

indicators.note: a special version of something is made differently, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A preconception about a special journey across a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: A parti pris, French for 'side taken', is a prejudice or opinion formed in advance.

clue.text: Claudio always on time through two days and one more

indicators.note: in an across clue one thing on another follows it
something passing through another sits inside it

parts.note: Monday is MON and day is D, the first of the pair split round the rest
T is the abbreviation for time
ever means always
the Roman numeral for one, added on

explanation.surface: Someone called Claudio is always punctual over a two-day stretch, and one more day after.
explanation.walkthrough: Claudio sounds like any man's name; it is the composer's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Claudio Monteverdi was the Italian composer of early opera such as Orfeo.

clue.text: Cross, missing most of bank holiday

indicators.note: most of the phrase that follows is left out, so only a short run of its letters is kept

parts.note: the run straddling the two words

explanation.surface: Someone grumpy at losing most of a public holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like the adjective for annoyed; it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: An ankh is the Egyptian looped cross, a symbol of life.

clue.text: General dropping on unprecedented bulletin

indicators.note: dropping something lets it fall away and leaves the rest

parts.note: general, shared by all
taken as written, the part removed
never seen before

explanation.surface: A general drops leaflets over enemy lines in an unprecedented propaganda drive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'General' looks like an army officer; it is the adjective meaning widespread.
explanation.definitionFit: A communiqué is an official announcement or statement issued to the press.

clue.text: A white child of the upper classes is left behind

indicators.note: being behind something means coming after it

parts.note: ch. is the abbreviation for child
A and B are the top social grades in British market research
L is the abbreviation for left
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pale-skinned posh child is abandoned.
explanation.walkthrough: In UK marketing, social grades A and B are the upper and middle classes. 'A white' is not a person but a white wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Chablis is a dry white wine from Burgundy, so it is one example of a white.

clue.text: Better being dealt with humbly

parts.note: to cap is to better or outdo
a matter in hand is being dealt with

explanation.surface: Being dealt a better card in a game, and accepting it modestly.
explanation.definitionFit: Going with your hat in your hands is to approach someone deferentially, as in begging.

clue.text: Irish girl in hospital in Bosnia with convulsions

indicators.note: something in another sits inside it
convulsions are violent jerks, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: An Irish girl lies in a Bosnian hospital having fits.
explanation.definitionFit: Siobhan is a common Irish female first name, the Gaelic form of Joan.

clue.text: Hercules, say, one sent to prison in mythical time

parts.note: Hercules is an example of a hero
the Roman numeral for one
a cage confines like a prison

explanation.surface: Hercules being jailed in some legendary era.
explanation.definitionFit: The heroic age is the legendary period of Greek myth when demigods like Hercules lived.

clue.text: They strum quietly before tragic heroine executed

indicators.note: execution takes off the head, so the first letter is dropped
one thing before another comes first in the answer

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical mark for quiet
Electra is the Greek tragic heroine who avenged her father

explanation.surface: Musicians play softly before a heroine of tragedy is put to death.
explanation.definitionFit: Plectra, plural of plectrum, are picks used to pluck guitar strings.

clue.text: A smack on the bottom for false charge

definitions.meaning: first meaning taken literally: a slap to the backside
second meaning: an unjust accusation, as in American slang

explanation.walkthrough: Bum is British for backside, so read literally the answer is a slap there; as an idiom it is a wrongful accusation.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means being blamed or convicted unfairly, while its words literally describe a slap on the behind.

clue.text: Army section sound busy — I agree to return

parts.note: a busy place or bee hums

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the words are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: sure! means I agree

explanation.surface: A military unit makes a racket and someone agrees to go back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Army' means military but is read as arm-y: a section of the arm.
explanation.definitionFit: The humerus is the long bone of the upper arm, so it is a part of an arm.

clue.text: Hated to change potentially exciting meeting

indicators.note: to change something is to alter its form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone loathed the idea of altering what might be a thrilling appointment.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot date is a romantic outing with an attractive person, promising excitement.

clue.text: Apparently noisy food

wordplay.note: with no call for silence (sh) a place is noisy, read as two words

explanation.surface: A dish that seems loud.
explanation.walkthrough: Split it as NO SH: where nobody says 'sh', things are evidently noisy.
explanation.definitionFit: Nosh is informal British slang for grub or a meal.

clue.text: Ancient wood and a little metal in old instrument

parts.note: shaw is an archaic word for a thicket or small wood

indicators.note: a little of a word is just a small piece of it, here its first letter

parts.note: the opening letter of metal

explanation.surface: An antique woodwind instrument with some metal fittings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wood' suggests woodwind, fitting the surface, but it is a stand of trees.
explanation.definitionFit: The shawm is a medieval double-reed woodwind, ancestor of the oboe.

clue.text: Archbishop given porridge not a moment too soon

parts.note: Justin Welby, former Archbishop of Canterbury
porridge is British slang for a prison sentence, doing time

explanation.surface: A churchman served a breakfast of oats.
explanation.walkthrough: Porridge is British slang for time spent in prison, from the sitcom of that name.
explanation.definitionFit: Just in time means arriving at the last possible moment, as is also the clue's phrase.

clue.text: Making a stand, wife deserts sly type

indicators.note: one who deserts leaves, so that letter goes missing

parts.note: a weasel is a sly, sneaky person
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A wife takes a stand and walks out on her sly partner.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is a frame or stand holding a painting or board upright.

clue.text: Cliff is no end frightening

indicators.note: with no end the final letter is dropped

parts.note: frightening means scary

explanation.surface: A precipice that is endlessly terrifying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cliff' could be a man's name; it is a rocky face.
explanation.definitionFit: A scar is a steep rocky outcrop or cliff on a hillside, especially in northern England.

clue.text: It stumps our cousin: he did you?

definitions.meaning: surface: something that baffles a relative; setter's reading: a tree that puzzles a monkey, our primate cousin
setter's second reading: a man who puzzled solvers, the famous Guardian setter of this pen-name

explanation.walkthrough: The tree's common name is monkey puzzle, so it stumps a monkey; the same name was used by John Graham, the much-loved Guardian setter, who baffled readers.
explanation.definitionFit: Araucaria is the botanical genus of the monkey puzzle tree and the pseudonym of a famous Guardian compiler.

clue.text: Courts large family all at once

definitions.meaning: second meaning: quadruplets, four children born together

explanation.walkthrough: 'Courts' suggests law courts or wooing, but it is courtyards.
explanation.definitionFit: The short form stands both for quadrangles enclosed by buildings and for quadruplets born at one birth.

clue.text: Not quite sober, show dissent

indicators.note: not quite all of a word means its last letter is cut

parts.note: demure means sober and modest

explanation.surface: A drinker, a little tipsy, protests.
explanation.definitionFit: To demur is to raise an objection or express reluctance.

clue.text: Sandwich and more substantial fare, a bit at a time

parts.note: piece is Scottish and northern English for a sandwich
a full meal is bigger than a snack

explanation.surface: Eating a snack and then a full dinner, gradually.
explanation.walkthrough: In Scotland a piece is a sandwich or packed lunch.
explanation.definitionFit: Piecemeal means done gradually, in stages rather than all together.
